notes: Clean slice-plus-claimed-map fix with a defensive append-aliasing fix, but parent override is still per config resource, and the new unit test locks in dropping the child's unrelated `q` instance.
Fixes the main case, but its new unit test locks in the child's b["q"] import being dropped because the parent targets b["p"], which is a silent drop.
Linear scan for overriding statements from other modules; fixes the repro but retains the per-config-resource cross-module drop, and the plan test only covers the root-module case.
Uses a quadratic linear scan to keep same-module blocks; cross-module override is still per resource, so child instances not targeted by the parent lose their imports.
Map-of-slices approach identical in effect to C1; it fixes the repro but not instance-level cross-module dedup.
Same map-of-slices approach as C3; fixes the issue scenario but keeps resource-granular parent override.

Keeps all same-module blocks via a map of slices, so the reported single-module case is fixed, but a parent block targeting one instance still silently drops a child module's blocks for every other instance of that resource.
Groups statements per resource in a map of slices; works for the reported case, but override is still per resource, and the existing[0] indexing is a bit awkward.
Same config-resource-level owner approach; it fixes the issue repro, but its unit test explicitly codifies dropping the child's `c` instance even though the parent never targets it.
Thorough unit test, but it explicitly asserts that the child's overridden["c"] import is discarded, codifying a silent drop.
Compares static instance keys so parent and child can import different instances, but falls back to over-dropping when keys are dynamic, and re-parses HCL addresses inside the refactoring package.

Moves toward per-instance override by statically re-parsing To addresses, but compares only the resource key (ignoring module instance keys) and conservatively drops blocks with dynamic keys, at the cost of extra parsing complexity.
Pointer-to-slice variant of the owner-map approach; fixes the single-module bug but keeps the coarse config-resource-level parent override.
Tracks which module owns each resource; drops all child blocks for a resource once a parent claims it, instead of overriding per instance as the reference does.
Uses a string-keyed Go map instead of addrs.Map for ownership, and the module-level override still drops child imports of other instances; it adds a reasonable unit test plus a plan test.
Uses a string-keyed Go map instead of addrs.Map, which is less idiomatic; same per-resource override limitation.
Same O(n^2) scan approach as C8; resolves the reported case only and leaves the cross-module silent drop.
Linear-scan variant like C4; fixes the issue scenario but keeps resource-level override across modules.

Returns every statement ordered child-before-parent and relies on knownImports.Put overwriting to get instance-level parent precedence, matching the reference behavior with minimal change, though the ordering coupling is implicit and the parent-override path is untested.

Minimal fix: removes config-level dedup and orders children before parents so the existing last-write-wins Put in expansion gives parent precedence per instance; correct, but relies on implicit overwrite semantics, and the test does not cover the cross-module override.
Concise owner-map fix that handles the issue's root-module scenario but keeps the coarse parent-overrides-all-child-blocks semantics.
Clean owner-map fix for same-module blocks; cross-module override remains per resource rather than per instance.
Owner-map fix with a plan test that also covers multiple blocks in a child module, but the parent override is still per config resource rather than per instance.
Owner-map approach with a good test covering a child module; still loses non-overlapping child instance imports when the parent targets the same resource.
Pointer-slice owner-map variant with an aliasing fix; it fixes the repro but not instance-level dedup across modules.
Pointer-slice owner-map approach that also fixes append aliasing; same resource-granular override limitation.
Owner map keeps same-module blocks and fixes the repro, but cross-module override still discards a child's imports of other instances; tests cover only the simple cases.

Fixes same-module for_each imports, but a parent block still overrides every child block for that resource, so child imports of other instances are silently dropped (the same class of bug as the issue).
Complete fix, but the parser wrapper helpers are tacked onto the end of parse.go; tests mostly assert only that there is no error and the segment count.
Correct fix via Token helpers, plus thin parser wrapper methods awkwardly appended after the var block; tests cover the main quoted-brace cases and dispenser argument behavior.

Misses the nested branch of NextBlock, so a quoted `{` or `}` ending a line still changes nesting when NextSegment walks nested blocks (e.g. handle { route { respond "}" } }); its tests check only site keys and miss this.
Correct via Dispenser helpers with some inline checks; the TestParseAll addition verifies only keys, not segment contents, so testing is weaker.
Correct, complete fix mixing Dispenser helpers with inline checks; tests are minimal (three table entries) with no nested-block coverage.
Correct, using Dispenser helpers plus inline checks for raw token variables (slightly inconsistent); tests are only a few segment-count cases added to an existing table.
Correct and complete, but repeats an inline `&& !Quoted()` at every site instead of adding a helper; tests are only a few table entries.
Correct, but repeats `Val()=="x" && !Token().Quoted()` inline everywhere instead of a helper, which hurts maintainability; tests are reasonable.
Complete fix with Token and Dispenser helpers (keeps the redundant wasQuoted check); comprehensive tests including unbalanced-brace errors, a nested route, a snippet and an adapt file.
Token plus bounds-checked Dispenser helpers, leaving the redundant wasQuoted check; very thorough tests including unbalanced-brace errors, snippets, and an adapt fixture.
Covers every structural brace check in the dispenser and parser through Token helper methods; it leaves a now-redundant wasQuoted check in directive(), and its dispenser and parse tests are solid.

Adds Token-level unquoted brace helpers and applies them at every structural brace check; it leaves the now-redundant wasQuoted check in directive() and has good dispenser and parse tests, including snippets.
Clean, complete fix with Token helpers and the redundant check removed; thorough tests cover segments, an unclosed-block error, snippets/import blocks and an adapt test.

Clean Token helpers applied consistently and the redundant check is removed; tests are thorough, covering parse cases, a quoted '}' failing to close the block, snippets/import blocks, and an adapt fixture.
Complete fix (addresses() uses an inline check instead of the new helper); a strong dispenser test checks nesting and cursor landing, plus table and server integration tests.
Correct and consistent apart from one inline check in addresses(); tests are strong (dispenser nesting/landing, parse cases), though the extra live-server integration test is heavier than needed.
Clean, complete fix with Token and Dispenser helpers and the redundant check removed; tests are reasonable table entries, including a nested block.
Same clean design as C11; table tests cover a quoted '{' as an argument before a real block and a quoted '}' inside it.
Clean Token-method fix, essentially identical in structure to C1, with the redundant check removed; tests are table entries only.
Consistent Token helpers with the redundant check removed, closely matching the reference; table tests include nested blocks after a quoted brace.
Complete fix with Token helpers and `at*Brace` Dispenser wrappers; a thorough dispenser test checks args, block contents, nesting and the follow-up token.
Clean Token helpers plus bounds-checked Dispenser atOpenBrace/atCloseBrace used consistently; good dispenser test and table cases.
Complete fix; its dispenser test usefully covers a lone quoted `}` that NextBlock iterates over without consuming args.
Clean, consistent helpers; tests include a quoted '}' alone on its own line inside a block, which is a nice edge case.

Complete fix using Token helpers plus Dispenser wrappers (the wrappers' bounds checks duplicate what Token() already does); good segment-level tests, though the dispenser test collects an unused `got` slice.
Consistent Token and Dispenser helpers with the redundant check removed; solid segment-content tests including backticks and snippet import.
Complete, but uses Dispenser-only helpers mixed with inline wasQuoted checks and keeps the redundant check; tests are decent, though the dispenser test can index-panic.
Correct, using Dispenser helpers but inline checks in addresses/doImport and a leftover redundant check; good parse and dispenser tests, though the snippet test only checks counts.
Correct transform, but it always marks exec as explicitly 'default', and tests cover unit and archive paths without an actual `k6 run --once` execution test.
Clean internal/cmd implementation close to the reference structure; the tests cover unit logic and archive output but have no end-to-end run test, and lower-layer shortcut handling is missing.
Works, but it puts a CLI-flag error constructor in the executor package, always sets exec as valid, and its tests are thin and sloppy (concatenated stderr+stdout+logs, only one conflict flag).

Works, but it puts a CLI-specific OnceConflictError helper into the public lib/executor package, the if/else-if debug-log flow is awkward, and the tests concatenate stderr, stdout and logs to find errors.

Applies a clean executor.ApplyOnce after consolidation, with flags on run, archive and cloud run and solid unit and integration tests; like every candidate, it misses the lower-layer (env/config) shortcuts that can wipe script scenarios before --once runs.
Works, but the integration tests are thinner (only --iterations is checked for conflicts, and tags/env are not verified), there is no archive test, and ApplyOnce is exported from lib/executor.
Concise and correct implementation with adequate but light tests: one conflict case and no archive test.

Applies --once correctly after consolidation and rejects the four CLI shortcuts, but misses execution-segment conflicts and env/config-layer shortcuts that wipe scenarios, and it adds a public ApplyOnce to lib/executor.

Correct ApplyOnce after consolidation, with conflict validation done early in loadAndConfigureLocalTest (split across two places) and thorough run, archive and unit tests; lower-layer shortcuts are not dropped.

Comprehensive tests, including immutability, default exec, multi-flag conflicts and archive; however validation and application are split across loadAndConfigureLocalTest and consolidate, and the logic lives in public lib/executor.

Self-contained cmd/once.go that checks conflicts from parsed CLI options, reports sorted scenario names and sets exit codes; strong unit, run and archive tests, though the BaseConfig override is slightly convoluted.

Self-contained internal implementation with a sorted-name ambiguity error and exit codes; very thorough unit, integration and archive tests, though env-layer shortcuts that clear scenarios are not handled.
Clean getOnce plus ApplyOnce with the flag on run, archive and cloud, and extensive tests covering metrics tags/env, setup/teardown and archive metadata; shares the lower-layer shortcut gap.
Good tests covering exec, env and tags via a custom counter, setup/teardown, all conflicts and archive; the logic sits in public lib/executor and lower-layer shortcuts are not handled.
Correct and well tested, but it hand-rolls countOccurrences instead of using strings.Count and leaves the deprecated `k6 cloud` command without the flag.
Correct wiring that includes cloud_run and archive with good tests, but it reinvents strings.Count in the tests and adds exported executor API.
Well-factored once.go (request, validate, apply), with the flag on run, archive and cloud and thorough unit, integration and archive tests.
Clean internal implementation with separate validation and apply steps, plus well-rounded unit, integration and archive tests; it shares the common gap of not dropping env/config shortcuts.
A single applyOnceFlag cleanly handles detection, conflicts, the sorted-name multi-scenario error and the transform; tests are comprehensive (unit no-op case, tags via JSON output, archive metadata).

A single cohesive internal applyOnceFlag registered on run, archive and cloud, with thorough unit, integration and archive tests; the archive assertion is slightly convoluted and env-layer shortcuts are unhandled.
Minimal and correct (flag in optionFlagSet, ApplyOnce in the executor package), with good integration and unit tests but no archive test and a redundant sum helper.
Clean ApplyOnce with good integration checks of env, scenario name and tags, but it duplicates the existing sum helper, has no archive test, and adds public executor API.
Solid ApplyOnce with good integration tests (including a startTime-discard check and setup/teardown counts) but no archive coverage.

Solid post-consolidation transform with good integration tests (startTime dropped, setup/teardown), but it exposes ApplyOnce publicly in lib/executor, has no archive test, and does not handle lower-layer shortcuts.
Correct, but the logic is crammed into config.go, exec is always explicit 'default', and the archive test only covers the no-scenario case.
Functionally fine, but the helpers are scattered across config.go and options.go while the test file is named once_test.go, and the archive test only covers the default scenario.
Works and is tested including archive, but it introduces an unnecessary new error type and isOnceSet silently swallows flag errors.
Adds an unnecessary exported OnceScenarioError type and DeriveOnceScenarios API, and isOnceSet swallows flag errors; otherwise correct with reasonable tests.
Queries the internal treePages per segment and applies slugs to regular pages only when their dir equals the section base, so pages in non-section subdirs are missed; fails a hidden test.

Looks up slugs through the internal treePages, and for regular pages only swaps the dir when it equals the section base, so pages in non-section subdirectories of a slugged section keep the old URL; this is consistent with the hidden test failure.
Works via a lowercased prefix map, but ToLower matching can mismatch unnormalized paths under DisablePathToLower; it also has a needless always-nil error return and type assertion.

Correct prefix-based replacement using separate SectionBase and ContainerDir fields; it has an error return that is always nil, slightly awkward duplication, and the same lowercase-matching caveat as C1.
Correct prefix-map replacement with separate SectionBase/ContainerDir overrides; ToLower matching is imprecise with DisablePathToLower, and it allocates a map for every page.
Correct prefix matching over ancestor slugs, with self included for branch pages and home and standalone pages excluded; it is clean overall but allocates a map for every page.
Prefix-map slug replacement is correct, but it hijacks ExpandedPermalink to inject the path, which conflates permalink semantics and is fragile.
Its prefix-based slug replacement is correct, but it routes the result through ExpandedPermalink as if a permalink pattern applied, which is a hacky reuse of unrelated semantics.
Routes the computed path through the permalink/QueryUnescape path and replaces an entire multi-segment relative section path with the slug, losing intermediate directories.
Hijacks the permalink/ExpandedPermalink mechanism, which conflates semantics, and a slugged section whose relative path spans non-section dirs has all those segments replaced by the slug.
Uses the current section's slugged path as the container dir for regular pages, which drops intermediate directories and risks URL collisions; fails a hidden test.

Replaces a regular page's whole container dir with the slugged section path, so it loses non-section subdirectories; a slug also replaces multi-segment relative section paths entirely, and the hidden test fails.
Passes a section-path→slug map in the descriptor and applies exact prefix matches with consistent unnormalized keys; sound, if slightly heavier than needed.

Passes a slug map keyed by section path (respecting disablePathToLower) into the descriptor and applies it in CreateTargetPaths; this is correct but splits the logic across packages and puts a map in the descriptor.
Clean CurrentSection→Parent slug map with prefix matching that works for normal cases; lowercasing segments to match normalized paths is imprecise under DisablePathToLower.

Walks the CurrentSection→Parent chain and replaces matching segments by lowercased path-prefix lookup, so intermediate non-section dirs and taxonomy/term pages work; the lowercase key matching is slightly fragile when disablePathToLower is set and paths contain characters that normalization changes.

Replaces segments by index using SectionsEntries depth, so it handles gapped nested sections, pages in non-section subdirs, and unnormalized paths; tests are thorough (deep section, ugly URLs, taxonomy/term).
Positions slugs via SectionsEntries, which handles intermediate non-section dirs, and skips pages with a url set; its tests cover nested non-section dirs, ugly URLs and taxonomy/term slugs.
Correct slug map applied in CreateTargetPaths with consistent unnormalized keys, but it uses an unnecessary *pageState type assertion and inline logic.
Takes the same slug-map approach as C6 and is correct, but it uses an unchecked *pageState type assertion where sp.Slug() would suffice.
Concise index-based slug replacement walking CurrentSection→Parent, with clean cmp.Or fallbacks in CreateTargetPaths; tests cover non-section subdirs, nested slugs and taxonomy/term.

Replaces segments by their depth position, which is case-independent and correct for intermediate dirs; uses cmp.Or concisely, and the tests cover deep non-section dirs, nested slugged sections and untranslated terms.
Correct depth-indexed replacement equivalent to C2, with a good test; it also includes docs edits the task did not require.
Correct position-based replacement much like C3, with good tests including a plain non-section dir, but it also edits docs files the task did not require.
Rebuilds section paths from BaseNameNoIdentifier per section, so nested sections whose parent skips a non-section directory lose that directory (e.g. /help/sub/deep becomes /ayuda/deep).

Rebuilds the section path from each ancestor's BaseNameNoIdentifier, so once any slug is present it drops intermediate non-section directories between sections (e.g. /help/sub/deep becomes /ayuda/deep); its tests are mostly existence checks.
Ignores slugs for pages in non-section subdirectories and replaces whole multi-segment relative paths with the slug; fails a hidden test.
Silently skips slug application for pages not directly in their section's dir, giving inconsistent URLs, and collapses intermediate dirs for slugged sections; the hidden test fails.

Clever, minimally intrusive approach that lets the ReturnError ride inside ExecError; however a bare return in a partial yields nil instead of the rendered output, try swallows return, and it rewrites `return A | B` rather than rejecting it.
Relies on the ReturnError flowing through ExecError wrapping, which is hacky; `try` swallows returns, bare return discards output, and it rewrites `return A | B` into an invented pipeline semantics.

Least intrusive to exec.go (relies on ExecError wrapping) with correct bare-return output semantics, but there is no trap at template/block boundaries and try swallows return; it also edits the forked parse/node.go.

Partial semantics are right, but nothing traps returns at template boundaries, so a return inside a `block`/`define` ends the whole template; `try` swallows returns and the change edits the forked parse package.

Correct semantics with try guard, arg validation and type-aware wrapping, plus an excellent unit test in texttemplate; but it is more intrusive, changing the Executer interface and the executeWithState signature in the fork.

Thorough: HasValue semantics, `try` passthrough, template-boundary trap, arg-count check, and both unit and integration tests; it adds a method to the Executer interface, but only lacks the reference's error paths.
No template-boundary trap, so a return in a block or define kills the parent render; keeps the old HasReturn discard semantics, and arg wrapping only applies in partials.
No template-boundary trap, so a return in any sub-template exits the whole execution, and a bare return in a partial yields nil; it does include a unit test.
Clean implementation with HasValue semantics, template trap, arg grouping and validation, plus good tests and docs; try does not re-panic the return, so `try (return x)` swallows it.
Matches the reference semantics well (HasValue, rendered output on bare return, block/template trap) with good tests and docs, but does not stop `try` from swallowing a return.
Clean recoverReturn helper, template-boundary trap and try handling, but it keeps the HasReturn discard-output semantics (bare or unreached return yields nil); good tests and docs.
Clean `recoverReturn` helper and `try` handling with good tests, but it keeps the old 'partials with return never render' semantics, so bare or fall-through returns yield nil.
Matches the reference semantics well (HasValue, template trap, try guard, arg grouping) with good tests including try; no arg-count validation, plus a small unrelated `return c, nil` tweak.

Correct HasValue semantics, template-boundary trap, `try` passthrough and good tests; it moves `return` to the templates namespace, has no arg-count check, and includes a slightly inaccurate doc line.

Solid sentinel design: walkTemplate traps the return, try re-panics it, a bare return yields the rendered output, extra args are rejected and legacy `return f a b` is grouped; misses the reference's pipeline-position error and edits exec.go directly instead of going through the fork script.
Correct HasValue semantics, template-boundary trap and `try` passthrough with good tests, but it moves `return` from the partials namespace to the templates namespace without updating docs.
Simple sentinel with template trap and try guard, but no arg grouping (legacy `return add 1 2` breaks), a bare return yields nil, and the field name Val is inconsistent.
Has the template trap and `try` handling, but drops support for `return fn args` without parentheses, and a bare return in a partial yields nil instead of the rendered output.
Has the template trap and errors.As handling, but drops `return f a b` grouping, which breaks the widely used legacy syntax; it also keeps the HasReturn discard semantics and has no try guard.
Does not wrap `return add 1 2`, a regression on previously supported syntax; `try` swallows returns and a bare return in a partial yields nil.
No template-boundary trap and a bare return yields nil; it rewrites `return A | B` into a grouped pipeline and redefines the 13600 regression test to expect success.
No template-boundary trap and bare return yields nil; it also turns `return x | f` into returning the whole pipeline and rewrites an existing regression test to match.
Correct core semantics (template-boundary trap, HasValue so a bare return yields output, arg grouping) with docs and a broad test; but try is not guarded and extra args are silently ignored.

Sound sentinel approach: bare return keeps the partial's rendered output, returns are trapped at template boundaries, and `return f a b` is wrapped; however `try` swallows a return, and there are no errors for a valued return outside partials or a non-final return in a pipeline.
No trap at the template/block boundary, so a return inside `define "main"` ends the whole baseof render; a bare return in a partial also yields nil instead of the output.
Returns are not trapped at `template`/`block` boundaries, so a return in a baseof `main` block truncates the whole page; a bare return in a partial yields nil and tests are thin.

Keeps the old HasReturn behaviour, so any partial containing a return discards its output even when the return is never reached and a bare return gives nil; the trap, try handling and conditional arg wrapping are otherwise reasonable.

Template-boundary trap, `try` passthrough and arg wrapping are clean, but it keeps the HasReturn discard semantics, so a bare return (or a fall-through) in a partial yields nil instead of the rendered output.
Correct and close to the reference, but adds a clunky extra parenPos parameter (0 passed in the unwrapped call) and omits the Pretty fix.
Has a reference-like wrapDurationExpr helper, but it adds a parenPos argument that duplicates the wrapped bool and is passed as 0 elsewhere; no Pretty fix.
Minimal correct fix via a helper and a recursive unary call, with a redundant range check, no Pretty fix and only basic tests.

Wraps the bare literal in a Wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr in both paren paths, as the reference does; it does not update Pretty, and the wrapped node's StartPos in -(N) points at the operator rather than the paren.
Wraps the bare literal in a unary-plus DurationExpr in both the paren and offset-unary paths and matches the reference's Pretty fix; the parse-time positive check only catches `(N)`, not `-(N)`.
Close to the reference and includes the Pretty unary-plus fix; it also keeps the parse-time error for foo[(0)], tested, though -(N) in a range is only caught at runtime.
Correct wrapping and keeps the positive and div/mod parse-time checks, but adds no tests for those preserved validation paths.
Correct wrapping and extended constant checks for range, division and modulo, but adds no tests for those error paths and no Pretty fix.
Works, but adds a public Wrapped field to NumberLiteral and mixes it with a separate unary-plus conversion, giving two representations and a more invasive AST change.

Adds a public Wrapped field to NumberLiteral and then also wraps it in an unwrapped unary-plus DurationExpr, which is a convoluted dual representation; it does keep the parse-time zero and division checks, but the change touches ast.go, printer.go and several grammar rules.
Cleanest reference-like fix: one helper used in both the paren and unary paths, redundant code removed, plus an evaluation test via durationVisitor; no Pretty change.
Cleanest reference-like refactor, using a single wrap helper in both paths, plus a useful durationVisitor evaluation test; Pretty is left printing (+5).
Thorough: includes the Pretty fix, positive-duration validation and evaluation/AST tests, though the unchecked `$2.(*NumberLiteral)` assertion is fragile.
Includes the Pretty fix, parse-time checks and rich tests, but paren_duration_expr does an unchecked $2.(*NumberLiteral) assertion that is fragile against future grammar changes.
Fixes the round-trip but also eagerly computes Range/Step/Offset, rewrites the matrix/subquery actions and addOffsetExpr, and changes subquery step print precedence, which is well beyond the issue.
Overreaches by setting both Range/Offset and their Expr fields for constants and changing the subquery step printing order, which alters AST invariants beyond what the issue requires.
Minimal and correct, but the wrapper's StartPos is the literal rather than the opening paren, and there is no Pretty fix or validation preservation.
Minimal and correct wrapping in both places; it lacks the Pretty fix and the parse-time positive/zero checks for parenthesised literals.
Adds a public Wrapped field to NumberLiteral with special-casing in offset_expr and positive_duration_expr; it works but is more invasive and less uniform than the reference.
Adds a NumberLiteral.Wrapped field and special-cases offset_expr; foo[-(5)] and 4d/-(0) slip past the parse-time checks, and the AST representation is mixed.
Correct wrapping, and keeps parse-time positive-duration and div/mod-by-zero checks for wrapped constants, with error and evaluation tests; no Pretty change.
Works and keeps the zero and positive checks with good tests, but builds the DurationExpr inline in two places instead of a helper; no Pretty fix.
Wraps literals with the paren position in both paths and keeps the positive-duration check, with good error and evaluation tests; div/mod checks are not updated.
Solid wrapping plus a preserved parse-time positive check, with good parse-error, round-trip and promqltest evaluation tests; Pretty is not updated.
Correct and keeps the validations, but replaces the bool parameter with an awkward *Item pointer and includes a stray change to the generated-file header.

Thorough constant-value checks for range, division and modulo with tests, but it changes the goyacc header line in the generated file, which would fail the generated-parser check, and uses an awkward *Item flag parameter.
Sound wrap-before-unary approach that keeps the parse-time positive check for wrapped constants; div/mod-by-zero checks are not updated and Pretty is not fixed.
Clean helper with accurate lparen positions and a recursive constant check for positive durations; no Pretty fix and no new error tests.
